facts.statement: Jagorina pandora is a species of rhenanid placoderm found in Upper Frasnian Germany.
facts.quote: Jagorina pandora is a rhenanid placoderm of Upper Frasnian Germany.

facts.statement: Jagorina pandora was a flattened, skate-like fish covered in armor made of unfused tubercles.
facts.quote: As with other rhenanids, it was a flattened, skate-like fish protected in an armor made up of unfused tubercles

facts.statement: Fossils of Jagorina pandora consist mainly of bone fragments and an intact skull.
facts.quote: Although J. pandora is known primarily from bone fragments and an intact skull

facts.statement: Jagorina pandora provides the primary details regarding the skull anatomy of rhenanids.
facts.quote: It is from Jagorina that the details of the skull anatomy of rhenanids are known.

facts.statement: Jagorina belongs to the parent group Asterosteidae.
Jagorina is classified within the family Asterosteidae.
Jagorina is a member of the class Placodermi.
Jagorina lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species was described by Jaekel in 1921.
rejected.quote: Jagorina pandora is a rhenanid placoderm of Upper Frasnian Germany.

rejected.statement: Jagorina pandora hunted smaller fish by ambushing them from the sea bottom.
rejected.quote: and preyed on other, smaller fish by ambushing them from the sea bottom.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'smaller fish by ambushing them from the sea'
